Inventory node/GPU/NIC placement and affinity, PCIe/NVLink paths, firmware and software versions, MTU, transport, registration permissions, GPU-direct support, message-size distribution, concurrency, clocks, and workload; mark estimates separately from facts. Define a falsifiable hypothesis: for the same placement and workload, with an interleaved matched non-RDMA or host-staging control, the verified RDMA path reduces p50 and p95 communication time by at least 10% without increasing p99 step time, CPU saturation, retries, timeouts, link errors, or application-level correctness failures. Change one reversible variable at a time in a canary, verify collective/data correctness, and roll back on a predeclared tail-latency regression, timeout/retry storm, link failure, or correctness error. corrected_answer: For this cluster_performance case, assume a multi-node GPU workload with RoCE enabled, but verify every platform fact before prescribing changes. Inventory node/GPU/NIC topology and affinity, PCIe/NVLink paths, switch port and priority mapping, firmware/driver/library versions, MTU, link speed, queue-pair count, message-size and concurrency distributions, clocks, and whether the application has silently fallen back to another transport. Explain the path from the collective library through verbs work requests/completions, registered host or GPU memory, queue pairs, NIC, switch fabric, and peer; distinguish GPU-direct from host staging and application communication time from NIC counters. Check PFC/ECN and priority-group configuration, buffer and pause behavior, route symmetry, MTU consistency, congestion, drops, retries, retransmissions, queue depth, and error counters, correlating timestamps rather than treating any single counter as proof. Define a falsifiable hypothesis: under an interleaved matched baseline with the same placement, workload, warm-up, and sample count, correcting the identified congestion or path fault reduces p95/p99 collective latency by at least 10% without increasing median latency, timeout/retry/error rates, pause duration, link drops, CPU/GPU idle time, or application correctness failures. Measure end-to-end collective and step latency distributions, throughput, queueing, NIC/switch counters, PFC/ECN marks, completion status, and fallback selection in stated units; report uncertainty and confounders. Change one reversible variable at a time, first in an isolated canary, and preserve evidence. Roll back immediately on correctness failures, sustained timeouts, link instability, or a predeclared tail-latency regression; do not disable lossless controls or guess vendor-specific settings. Before claiming improvement, provide topology/configuration snapshots, synchronized traces, matched baseline results, and a validation run across representative message sizes and placements.
